summary.headline: Godrej Properties Q2 FY27 bookings fell 6% YoY to INR8,008 crore, but sustenance sales rose 83% to INR5,054 crore and collections hit INR5,318 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 bookings were INR8,008 crore from 3,658 units (6.2 mn sq ft), down 6% YoY and 7% QoQ, while H1 bookings grew 7% to INR16,669 crore. Sustenance sales were the standout at INR5,054 crore. Collections rose 31% YoY to a record Q2 of INR5,318 crore and operating cash flow was INR1,584 crore. Reported P&L fell sharply: EBITDA down 72% to INR171 crore and net profit down 62% to INR154 crore, which management attributed to back-ended deliveries and JV exit accounting (Mahalunge, Orris). Management guided H2 bookings of INR22,500-25,000 crore and a strong Q3 launch pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: INR8,008 crore (3,658 units, 6.2 mn sq ft)
INR16,669 crore (7,396 units, 12.3 mn sq ft)

segments.name: Geographic bookings Q2
segments.commentary: NCR just under INR2,000 crore, Mumbai about INR1,900 crore, Bangalore just under INR1,600 crore, Pune about INR1,000 crore, Hyderabad about INR700 crore, other cities about INR800 crore.

segments.name: Launches and projects
segments.commentary: Godrej Trilogy (Mumbai), Godrej Vanantara (Bengaluru), Godrej Samaris (Gurugram) and Godrej Brooklyn Avenue (Hyderabad) each contributed over INR500 crore to bookings. Four projects added in H1 with about 9 mn sq ft and about INR15,500 crore expected booking value, about 78% of FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 bookings guidance of INR22,500-25,000 crore; management said it expects to surpass full-year guidance across key operating metrics.
H2 cash collections of INR15,000 crore and operating cash flow of INR7,000 crore, with the company expecting to be free cash flow positive for the period.
Expects FY28 to show positive free cash flow and a 20% reported ROE.
Full-year delivery target of 13.5 mn sq ft; 2.5 mn sq ft delivered in Q2.
H2 launch pipeline of about INR32,000 crore; Q3 expected to be a very big sales quarter, with Bandra Bay and Godrej Verano (Golf Course Extension Road, slipped from Q2) as key launches.
Attributable share of sales was 85% in Q2 and 90% in H1.
capex_capacity: Q2 construction and related outflows up 31% YoY; H1 up 42% YoY to about INR1,292 crore. Management expects H2 construction pace to be equally strong, excluding NCR where the NGT ban limits activity.
Only about one-third of the annual launch pipeline was launched in H1; launches are picking up from October.

About 80% of Q3 approvals were secured before the quarter began; the residual is expected shortly after Diwali. For Q4, about 80% of approvals are targeted between end-November and mid-December, with the rest by mid-January.

Business development is opportunistic; threshold returns are a 20% IRR and a 15% bookings-to-net-profit margin. Bangalore and Noida are priority additions, plus select Mumbai micro-markets (South Mumbai, Western suburbs, Thane).
demand_pricing: Management said prices are holding up: less than 1% increase in some NCR projects, about 2% in South and Mumbai projects, and about 0.5% in the rest of the portfolio.
Godrej Crown Residences (Noida, Godrej Golf Links) saw a very large price jump; management said the cluster profit has almost tripled and the project is 88% sold.
Management said the company is not pushing price aggressively and is focused on end-user sales quality.
Sustenance was 60-40 vs launches historically; Q2 mix was 63% launch and 37% sustenance per management's framing of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA and net profit fall sharply despite higher sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra Khetawat said the Mahalunge JV became a 100% owned project after the partner exit, so the bulk of profit had been recognised earlier through DM fees and overheads, which led to near-equal sales and cost of sales. The Orris settlement also picked up losses on consolidation in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How long will sustenance sales stay high and what is the launch vs sustenance mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said H2 launches will likely outperform sustenance, and the 60-40 launch-sustenance mix is a guide that can flip if launches slip. Sustenance strength reflects a deliberate push after Gurgaon and Mumbai launches slipped.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company exceed its H2 sales guidance and how much can it add to pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said the top end of the H2 range (INR25,000 crore) would imply a 40% five-year compounded booking growth. He said the company will not hold back if opportunities arise beyond the 15-20% FY28 growth target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the H2 launch pipeline has approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of Q3 requirements were secured before the quarter, with the rest expected after Diwali. For Q4, management targets about 80% approvals by mid-December and the rest by mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on BD and competitive intensity for land?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said competition is ongoing but opportunities meeting return thresholds are available, and BD will remain opportunistic. Gaurav Pandey said one or two deals could close in the quarter if terms fit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near FCF-positive status in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said there is a high probability of being FCF positive in Q4 under aggressive internal scenarios, while noting this is not an obsessive target. FY28 is described as almost certain for operating cash flow guidance.

risks_watch: Q2 booking decline of 6% YoY and 7% QoQ, with H2 delivery dependent on launches clearing approvals on time (Q3 and Q4).
NCR construction constrained by NGT/GRAP restrictions; Mumbai air quality could create similar issues.
Macro risk: management was asked about Brent at $115/bbl and weaker equity markets; management said it sees no change in footfalls or conversions.
Profit volatility from JV exits (Mahalunge, Orris) and remaining 5-6 JVs to be exited, with lumpy one-off consolidation effects.
Brand and governance question raised by an investor on Godrej Splendour, Whitefield: booking revenue on OC while handover is delayed. Management said it will look into the case.
Execution of FY28 reported ROE of 20% and positive FCF depends on project completion accounting.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on sales momentum, cash collections and H2 pipeline, while openly acknowledging that the headline booking number and reported P&L were weak due to timing. Evasive on specific one-offs beyond general explanation, and on the Splendour question management deferred to a follow-up.
key_quotes: We only launched 1/3 of our expected annual launch pipeline in the first half of the financial year, and we're still able to deliver 43% of our annual bookings guidance, highlighting the continued strength of underlying demand in the sector.
Certainly, we do not believe in creating any gap between occupation certificate and actual delivery.
I don't think we believe in this sort of trying to just optically show a very, very steady performance.

growth.why: Management held H2 FY27 bookings guidance at INR22,500-25,000 crore, H2 collections at INR15,000 crore and 13.5 mn sq ft FY27 delivery; backing is a launch pipeline of about INR32,000 crore in H2 (four H1 projects worth about INR15,500 crore expected booking value, about 78% of FY27 guidance) and approvals, but no specific capacity additions and bookings were down 6% YoY in Q2.
